on-brass-deep-muted.displayName: Ink on Deep Brass, Second Line

display.purpose: The name on the first screen and the headline of the closing section. Uppercase.

headline.purpose: A section's name, alone, opening the section. Uppercase.

title.purpose: The name of a row that carries a paragraph: the capability domains, the featured channel. Uppercase.

lead.purpose: The one statement on the first screen, capped at 21em.

body.purpose: Prose, captions and table values. Paragraphs are capped between 34em and 44em.

term.purpose: The name of a thing a caption explains: a callout, a stack group, the record's title. Uppercase.

label.purpose: The label column of every ruled table and every table head. Uppercase, never a sentence.

control.purpose: Navigation, buttons, the language switch. Uppercase. The two load buttons track 0.14em.

field.purpose: A two-word fact set in a bordered field.

numeral.purpose: A measured figure in a readout, tabular so a changing number never moves its neighbours.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The header leaving and returning, and the burger.

motion.name: t-ui
motion.purpose: Every state change: background, border and colour only.

motion.name: theme-swap
motion.purpose: The theme changes in one frame with every transition held off; any fade of the themed surfaces restyled and repainted the whole page on every frame.

motion.name: header-hide
motion.purpose: The header leaves while the page scrolls down and returns on scroll up; it does both tens of times a visit, so both are short.

motion.name: row-reveal
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, y 22px to 0, 0.8s expo.out, 0.06s stagger, once
motion.purpose: Rows settle as they enter the viewport at 90% of its height.

motion.name: intro
motion.value: opacity and up to 20px of y, 0.7s to 1.1s expo.out, staggered over about 0.55s
motion.purpose: The first screen settling, once. There is no preloader.

motion.name: record
motion.purpose: The tick record: the only loop on the page. Stops off-screen and when the tab is hidden.

components.name: Project Door

narrative.overview:
The page is laid out as the technical sheet of a watch movement: what runs under the case-back, regulated and measured. It is a printed document, so it is built from the things such a sheet prints: ruled tables, numbered callouts on leader lines, a graduated ring, a dotted record, an exploded view, a train graph. Nothing on it is a picture of a movement. There are no gears and no cards.

Each theme is one material from top to bottom. Dark is graphite, a warm near-black drawn from the brass's own hue; light is a rhodium sheet with steel ink. Neither contains a neutral grey, a pure black or a pure white. Brass draws the rules, the numerals and the mark. Ruby is reserved for one meaning, a value being measured right now. Because meaning is carried by form before hue (solid, dashed, hollow), the sheet and the mark both survive in a single ink.

The density is that of a data sheet: tall condensed capitals for names, small tracked capitals for labels, a scientific serif for sentences, hairlines one pixel wide. It refuses the dark developer portfolio with one neon accent and a fake terminal, and it refuses that page's editorial-serif opposite. It is also quiet: the record of the tick is the only thing that loops, and nothing moves under the pointer.
keyCharacteristics: One ramp per theme: graphite in dark, rhodium in light, never mixed.
Brass is the signal; ruby is a live measurement and nothing else.
Every table opens on a brass rule and closes each row on a hairline.
Square corners on every box; circles only where the sheet draws an instrument or a reference.
Flat. Depth is four tones of one ramp, with no shadow and no blur.
Three faces with three jobs, and no mono face.
State by form: solid, dashed, hollow.
A number in a bubble always points into a figure.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: A theme is one ramp all the way down. Dark has no pale surface and light has no dark one; sections separate by elevation within the ramp, never by inversion.

rules.name: The Steel Ink Rule
rules.body: Steel is the ink of the light theme and nothing in the dark one. It is never a dark ground and never a dark hairline: thin saturated blue lines on warm black read as neon on black, which is the look this sheet refuses.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Ruby is only ever a value being measured now: the arc on the dial, the tick in the readout, the head of the record. It is never a hover, a status, a rule or an ornament, and it never touches the mark.

rules.name: The Discord Fill Rule
rules.body: A door or a cell filled with brass means Discord and nothing else: the project door on the first screen and the featured cell of the contact table. Every other primary action is filled with ink.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: No colour is written outside the token file, and text is never dimmed with opacity. A quieter voice is a quieter token; opacity is for animation state only.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Extra Condensed sets titles, Condensed sets labels, numerals and controls, the serif sets sentences. None does another's job, and there is no fourth face.

rules.name: The Name Alone Rule
rules.body: A section opens on its name alone. No kicker above a heading and no number beside one.

rules.name: The Capitals Rule
rules.body: Capitals belong to the condensed faces and to names, labels and controls. A sentence is never set in capitals and the serif is never tracked.

rules.name: The Brass Head Rule
rules.body: Every table and list opens on a brass rule 1.5px thick and closes each row on a 1px hairline. The label sits in a narrow left column, the value beside it.

rules.name: The Reference Rule
rules.body: A number in a bubble is a reference into a figure. Where the figure or its leader lines are not drawn, the numbers go with them.

rules.name: The Empty Cell Rule
rules.body: A field with no data stays empty. Nothing is written to balance a row.

rules.name: The Printed Sheet Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no blur, no gradients. The fixed header takes a flat scrim of its own ground when it floats; a frosted bar would be the one piece of glass on a printed page.

rules.name: The Well Rule
rules.body: An instrument sits in a well, one step below the sheet: the dial, the tick record, the career diagram, the foot of the page. Raising is reserved for something to press.

rules.name: The Square Box Rule
rules.body: Every box has square corners. A circle means an instrument or a reference: the dial, a callout bubble, a node, a leader's terminal.

rules.name: The Form First Rule
rules.body: State is carried by form, never by hue alone. A control that cannot act goes dashed; work is a solid run and study a hollow one; the stretch with no employer on the record is dashed rather than left off.

rules.name: The Still Pointer Rule
rules.body: Hover is background, border and colour. Nothing translates, scales or tilts under the pointer, and hover styling applies only where the device can hover.

rules.name: The Measured Figure Rule
rules.body: Every figure in a readout is measured at runtime. A decorative number is not a component of this system.

dos: Do build each theme from one ramp: the graphite ramp for dark, the rhodium ramp for light, mapped onto the same roles.
Do open every table and list on a 1.5px brass rule and close each row on a 1px hairline.
Do fill a primary action with ink (`--fg`) and outline its partner in `--fg-muted` at 1px; both are at least 44px tall.
Do keep the brass fill for Discord: one door on the first screen, one cell at the foot.
Do set labels in Sofia Sans Condensed 600 at 0.8125rem, uppercase, tracked 0.16em, in `--fg-subtle`.
Do set any number that changes in tabular figures.
Do put an instrument in a well (`--bg-sunken`) with a 1px hairline around it.
Do tell two states apart by form first: solid, dashed, hollow.
Do recompute the contrast table in the token file when a tone moves; every text tone clears 4.5:1 on both the sheet and the well in both themes.
Do draw a figure from data and at the width it is given, so its lettering stays the size it was set at.
Do use the A-quatro with the handle and the AS with the name, the drawing in one colour, from the files in `brand/`; off the page, use the lockup files there instead of setting the lettering again.
donts: Don't put a pale surface in the dark theme or a dark one in the light theme.
Don't bring blue into the dark theme, as a ground or as a hairline; steel is the light theme's ink only.
Don't swap the graphite for a neutral grey or a pure black; it carries the brass's hue.
Don't use ruby for a hover, a status, a rule or an ornament.
Don't fill a control or a cell with brass unless it is the Discord door or the Discord cell.
Don't write a colour outside the token file, and don't dim text with opacity.
Don't add a shadow, a blur, a gradient or a rounded corner to a box.
Don't put a kicker above a heading or a number beside one.
Don't number a list that has no figure to point into.
Don't draw a gear, a cog or a tourbillon; nothing on the sheet is a picture of a movement.
Don't add a mono face; nothing on the page is code.
Don't move, scale or tilt an interactive element on hover.
Don't add a preloader, a smooth-scroll library, a marquee or a second looping animation.
Don't use pixel lettering, pixel marks or any retro-game register.
Don't redraw, outline, slant, round or recolour the mark, don't set its lettering in another face, and don't set the two drawings side by side.
Don't show a number that is not measured or sourced.
